trackers.title: US Measles Tracker
trackers.description: Independent, sourced tracker of the 2026 US measles surge: CDC case counts, cases by state, outbreaks, deaths, elimination status and a dated timeline.

status.label: Growing · most since 1991
status.summary: CDC counted 4,852 confirmed cases as of 29 October, 264 more than in its previous update, with 511 hospitalisations and 43 new outbreaks reported in 2026. Pennsylvania's outbreak, centred on Lancaster County, has reached 1,398 cases in 44 counties, 265 hospitalisations and five confirmed deaths by the state's count (28 October), while CDC counts three, a figure it confirmed on 20 October. A regional health body will decide in November whether the US has lost the measles elimination status it has held since 2000.

trackers.headline: US measles cases reach 4,852, the most since 1991, CDC says. Pennsylvania's outbreak has reached 1,398 cases and New York has declared a disaster emergency.

latest.title: CDC: 4,852 cases, 264 more than last update

trackers.title: Ebola Tracker: DR Congo
trackers.description: Independent, sourced tracker of the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in DR Congo: confirmed cases and deaths, affected provinces, spread to other countries, vaccines, WHO risk and a dated timeline.

status.label: Growing · global health emergency
status.summary: DR Congo government data show the death toll has passed 5,000, with more than 10,000 people infected since the outbreak was declared in May, Reuters and Al Jazeera reported on 30 and 31 October. The Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak declared on 15 May has now reached 8 of DR Congo's 26 provinces: on 18 October the health ministry confirmed two cases, one fatal, in North Ubangi, AP reported. ECDC's latest update counts 10,274 confirmed cases and 4,992 deaths in DR Congo, from data up to 28 October. That is up from the 10,193 cases and 4,960 deaths in its update of 28 October (data to 27 October), the 10,141 cases and 4,928 deaths ECDC counted in its update of 27 October (data to 26 October), the 10,060 cases and 4,887 deaths DR Congo's public health institute (INSP) reported as of 25 October, passing 10,000 cases, according to Reuters and Al Jazeera, the 9,964 cases and 4,851 deaths ECDC counted in its update of 25 October (data to 24 October), the 9,816 cases and 4,757 deaths CDC lists as of 22 October and the 9,704 cases and 4,687 deaths WHO reported as of 20 October; ECDC's update of 19 October counted 66 of 178 health zones affected across the eight provinces (data to 17 October). CDC calls it the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record. Kenya's health ministry has confirmed nine cases, two of them fatal (the second death was announced on 23 October); three are health workers who cared for the first patient, and on 20 October the ministry said all nine belong to one cluster with no evidence of transmission outside it. On 26 October the ministry released the first 20 contacts from quarantine after 21 days of monitoring without symptoms, Reuters reported. On 20 October Nigeria confirmed one imported case in the Federal Capital Territory, in a person with recent travel to Uganda; WHO says where and when the person was exposed is not yet known. On 26 October the patient was evacuated to Switzerland, and NCDC said on 26 October that it was following 54 primary contacts. On 22 October CDC ordered that, from 3 November, all passengers boarding international flights to the United States attest that they have not been in DR Congo in the previous 21 days. There is no licensed vaccine for this strain; trials of an existing Ebola vaccine began in August, an early-phase trial of a Bundibugyo-specific candidate began in Uganda on 6 October, and on 23 October CEPI said the first participant had been vaccinated in the pivotal Tumaini trial in Bunia, DR Congo.

trackers.headline: DR Congo government data show Ebola deaths have passed 5,000, Reuters and Al Jazeera reported on 30 and 31 October. ECDC's latest count, from data up to 28 October, is 10,274 confirmed cases and 4,992 deaths. The outbreak is in eight provinces. Kenya has confirmed nine cases, two of them fatal, and Nigeria one imported case.

trackers.title: Mpox Tracker: Africa & World
trackers.description: Independent, sourced mpox tracker: WHO case counts for Africa, countries with active transmission, clade Ib spread in Europe and the US, vaccines, emergency status and a dated timeline.

status.label: Active · no global emergency
status.summary: WHO ended its global mpox emergency in September 2025, and Africa CDC lifted its continental emergency on 22 January 2026, but cases continue. WHO counted 1,153 confirmed cases and 7 deaths in 11 African countries in the six weeks to 16 August, 785 of them in Madagascar, where a clade Ib outbreak that began in December 2025 has passed 3,000 confirmed cases. Outside Africa, clade Ib is spreading locally in Europe, mostly among men who have sex with men, and CDC says sustained spread in the US is likely.

trackers.headline: WHO counted 1,153 confirmed mpox cases in 11 African countries in the six weeks to 16 August, most in Madagascar. CDC says sustained clade Ib spread in the US is likely.

trackers.title: Cholera Tracker: Global
trackers.description: Independent, sourced tracker of cholera worldwide in 2026: WHO case and death counts, countries reporting cases, how this year compares with 2025, WHO's risk level and a dated timeline.

status.label: Slowing · below 2025's pace
status.summary: WHO counted 275,284 cholera and acute watery diarrhoea cases and 2,601 deaths in 28 countries from 1 January to 30 August, 43% fewer cases and 58% fewer deaths than a year earlier, and August's cases fell 25% from July. Afghanistan, Nigeria and DR Congo report the most cases. WHO rated the global risk very high in June, and 2025 brought the most cholera deaths reported to WHO since 1999. ECDC's separate count reached 291,272 cases and 2,471 deaths by 27 October. In Zambia, the health minister told Parliament on 29 October that a new outbreak has reached 1,622 cases and 30 deaths since 28 July, in 20 districts across six provinces, according to local media.

trackers.headline: WHO counts 275,284 cases and 2,601 deaths in 28 countries by 30 August, 43% fewer cases than a year earlier. 2025 had the most deaths since 1999.

trackers.title: Dengue Tracker: Europe
trackers.description: Independent, sourced tracker of locally acquired dengue in Europe in 2026: ECDC and national case counts, affected countries and clusters, the yearly trend since 2010, vaccines and a dated timeline.

status.label: Active · local cases in Italy and France
status.summary: Italy and France are the only EU/EEA countries with locally acquired dengue this year. Italy's national health institute (ISS) counted 76 local cases by 27 October, up from 73 by 20 October, when they were linked to 5 outbreaks plus 2 cases not linked to the others, in places including the provinces of Livorno, Lecce and Milan and a cluster in Cartigliano (Vicenza) that had reached 8 cases by 2 October; Italy's National Blood Centre added Rome to its list of affected areas on 2 October. France counts 8 cases in 5 episodes (data to 26 October), with no new episode since its previous bulletin. The total is well below the 2024 record of 304. ECDC reports weekly until November.

trackers.headline: Italy has 76 locally acquired dengue cases this year and France 8, well below the 2024 record of 304.

latest.title: France: 8 local dengue cases in 5 episodes; local chikungunya at 205

trackers.title: Russia Plague Watch
trackers.description: Independent, sourced tracker of the suspected plague case in Irkutsk, Siberia: live incubation countdown, case counts, WHO risk level, claim check and a dated timeline.

status.label: Suspected, unconfirmed
status.summary: A 28-year-old worker at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute died overnight on 1–2 October after severe pneumonia. Media reports link the death to pneumonic plague. Russian authorities list the cause as "pneumonia of unknown etiology". On 6 October Russia told WHO that no dangerous pathogens were found in any contact tested. On 7 October WHO said it was still waiting for Russia to identify the pathogen and could not yet complete a full risk assessment. On 8 October the regional governor said the hospital quarantine had been lifted and that monitoring of all contacts was complete.

trackers.headline: Russian officials say quarantine at Shelekhov hospital is lifted and monitoring of all contacts is complete. Plague is not confirmed, and WHO is still waiting for Russia to name the pathogen.

latest.title: Governor says quarantine lifted and monitoring of all contacts complete
WHO asks Russia for the pathogen, test results and contact details

trackers.title: Marburg Watch
trackers.description: Independent, sourced Marburg tracker: any new cases in Africa, Uganda's isolated case in 2026, and the full record of Ethiopia's first outbreak (November 2025 to January 2026) with a dated timeline.

status.label: Watching · no new cases reported
status.summary: Uganda notified WHO of a confirmed Marburg case in Kyegegwa district on 30 June 2026: a young child who had died, found through surveillance set up for Ebola. Africa CDC said no contacts had developed symptoms, and no further cases have been reported since. Ethiopia's first outbreak, confirmed in Jinka on 14 November 2025, was declared over on 26 January 2026 after 42 days without a new case. WHO counted 14 confirmed cases, 9 of whom died, plus 5 probable cases who all died. Headlines saying Ethiopia's death toll is climbing date from December 2025.

trackers.headline: No further Marburg cases have been reported since Uganda's isolated case in late June. Ethiopia's first outbreak ended on 26 January with 14 confirmed cases and 9 deaths.

latest.title: Uganda reports a Marburg case in Kyegegwa
